newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Black says not a seller of Fairfax.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Black says not a seller of Fairfax.

text.p: Canadian media mogul Conrad Black said speculation his 25 percent stake in Australian newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd was on the market was false.
"Our enthusiasm for Fairfax and for raising our stake in it are undimmed," Black said in a statement.
Black added that he and his colleague Dan Colson had often stated they had no interest in staying permanently at 25 percent but were under no pressure to sell.

Late last month the Australian newspaper reported that Black was believed to be preparing to sell his Fairfax stake and said stockbroker Ord Minnett was understood to be sounding out fund managers which might be prepared to buy Fairfax stock.
Black also referred to comments by Australian communications minister Richard Alston in a recent television interview.

"Wildly inaccurate public musing by the minister of communications regarding the sale of our shareholding or the breakup of the Fairfax group is no more helpful to any legitimate interest than was the erratic conduct of some of his predecessors," Black said.
In a separate statement, Fairfax chairman Sir Laurence Street said it was to be regretted that Alston chose to speculate in the public domain.
"The speculation is unfounded and it has the potential to be destabilising both in the market place and amongst our staff. Fairfax is not hovering on the brink of dismemberment," he said.
The Australian government has said it will hold an inquiry into the media industry but as yet has not released details about the inquiry's terms of reference or timing.
Black's Hollinger International Inc hold its 25 percent stake in Fairfax through Britain's The Telegraph Plc.
Colson is deputy chairman of Fairfax and chief executive of The Telegraph.
Fairfax's other major shareholders are Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd with about 17 percent and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd with about five percent.
Both have expressed interest in gaining control of Fairfax.
